clue.text: Riders very cold in pre- Christian combat area

indicators.note: the word for very cold is placed inside the abbreviation for pre-Christian times

parts.note: BC, before Christ, marks dates before the Christian era
icy means very cold
the lists were the enclosed ground where knights jousted

explanation.surface: Horsemen fighting in a frozen arena in ancient times.
explanation.definitionFit: People who ride pedal bikes are riders of a sort, so the word fits.

clue.text: House of cards

parts.note: house is another name for the numbers game called housey-housey, played on printed cards marked off as numbers are called

explanation.definitionFit: The calling game was long known as house or housey-housey, and each player holds a card of numbers.

clue.text: After three, gets someone to find thequeen .

definitions.text: After three, gets someone to find thequeen

parts.words: After three, gets someone to find thequeen
parts.note: a conjuror shuffles three cards and asks a spectator to pick out the queen, as in find the lady

explanation.definitionFit: Finding the lady among three playing cards is a classic bit of sleight of hand with a pack.

clue.text: … in course of making her castle tours, perhaps

indicators.note: the words her castle tours are what the new arrangement is made out of

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a woman visiting castles, perhaps as part of a course.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the card-trick clue but adds nothing to the parse; a charlotte russe is a dessert, one course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlotte russe is a cold pudding of sponge fingers round a cream filling, served as the sweet course.

clue.text: Fancy I must have a drink inside me!

indicators.note: the drink with its article goes inside the word me

parts.note: gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming that they'd like a drink to be poured into them.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to picture it in the mind, the verb's sense of supposing.

clue.text: Huge number in a bird-raising operation

annotationWithheld.why: Huge number in a bird-raising operation: TIT and A and N are visible, but no reading of 'operation' gives IC, so the clue as held may be garbled
annotationWithheld.clue: Huge number in a bird-raising operation

clue.text: A right turn in a ship

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in a game

explanation.surface: Someone taking a right turn aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason sailed in the Argo in Greek myth, the most famous named vessel of legend.

clue.text: Macgillicuddy's high on smokes

definitions.meaning: Macgillycuddy's ... are the highest mountain range in Ireland, in County Kerry
to reek is to give off smoke or a strong smell

explanation.definitionFit: The Kerry range is named the Reeks, and reeking is giving off fumes, as a chimney does.

clue.text: it's more important to make the exits sound

indicators.note: sound tells us the words for exits are said out loud to give a different spelling

parts.note: out-ways are ways out, exits

explanation.surface: Advice that improving the emergency exits matters most.
explanation.definitionFit: If a thing carries greater weight in a decision it matters more than the rest, a figurative sense of heaviness.

clue.text: Change here, tell half or all out

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Instructions at a station to change trains and tell a partial or full crowd to get off.
explanation.definitionFit: Going all out means at full speed, which is what the idiom about riding hard means.

clue.text: Transport in rain-storm to Buddhist state

indicators.note: the vehicle goes inside the stirred-up letters of rain
a storm whirls things about, so the letters of rain are jumbled

parts.note: a van is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Travel through a downpour on the way to enlightenment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' makes NIRA from RAIN, and 'in' puts VAN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the release from desire and rebirth that Buddhists seek, a state of perfect peace.

clue.text: Menace envelops a quarter in that place

indicators.note: envelops means the word for menace wraps round a compass point

parts.note: a threat is a menace
east, E, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A threatening presence surrounding part of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned adverb meaning at that spot or on that account, close to there.

clue.text: 'Astronomical figure shown by error in till. Coo !

indicators.note: an error puts letters in the wrong order, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone exclaiming at an enormous sum shown by a mistake in the cash register.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Con', which leaves the letters one O short; 'Coo!', a British exclamation of surprise, gives exactly the needed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A one followed by many zeros, the kind of huge number found in astronomy.

clue.text: Thread is supplied In reverse measure

indicators.note: is supplied in means the word is placed inside the other piece
reverse tells us the word for a measure is turned backwards

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: Thread provided by a backwards-running length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' turns ELL into LLE, and 'supplied In' puts IS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, strong cotton yarn once used for stockings, a kind of thread.

clue.text: Mark of the merryman

definitions.meaning: Jack ... is the jester in Gilbert and Sullivan's The Yeomen of the Guard, singer of The Merryman and his Maid

explanation.definitionFit: A dot is a mark, and the Gilbert and Sullivan jester shares the surname.

clue.text: Theatre to indulge in 1dn?

parts.note: to play is to indulge in a game or pastime
the answer to 1 down is the calling game also known as house

explanation.surface: A theatre where one can enjoy the game from 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is a building for staging plays, another word for a theatre.

clue.text: Fencing long since needing repair

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A boundary fence that has long wanted mending.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing a field is surrounding it, shutting it in on every side.

clue.text: China's alternative, taken in China

parts.note: the rival to China tea is drunk from china cups, the second China being crockery

explanation.definitionFit: Assam and Darjeeling are the usual alternative to China leaf, and both are drunk from porcelain cups.

clue.text: Snow over-shoes ?

parts.note: snow lying deep enough to cover one's shoes, reaching the lower leg

explanation.definitionFit: Snow deep enough to cover the footwear reaches up to the joint above the foot.

clue.text: Australian digger could be chained

indicators.note: could be shows the letters of chained may become another word

explanation.surface: An Australian soldier who might end up shackled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digger' suggests an Australian soldier, but here it is a burrowing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The echidna, or spiny anteater, is an Australian mammal that burrows into soil with strong claws.

clue.text: Trees of part of London's dockland

definitions.meaning: tall, fast-growing trees of the willow family
Poplar is a district of East London by the old docks

explanation.walkthrough: The plural fits the trees; the London district is singular, and the S comes with the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The trees and the East London district share the name.

clue.text: Covers outside round swimming pools

indicators.note: outside means the word for covers goes round the ring-shaped letter

parts.note: lids are covers
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Covers placed round open-air pools.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming bath.

clue.text: Farm-worker with upper-class following in India

indicators.note: following shows the upper-class letter comes after the farm-worker

parts.note: a hind is an old word for a farm labourer

explanation.surface: A labourer with a posh retinue in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Farm-worker' tempts towards a deer or a hand, but HIND is the old Scots or northern farm servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Most people in India follow the country's majority faith, so a follower of it is typically found there.

clue.text: Steals, but has nothing to say

indicators.note: to say means the word for nothing is spoken out loud

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A thief who keeps silent about it.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, to nick something is to pinch or steal it.

clue.text: Chance the bunker? Not as planned

parts.note: hap is an old word for chance or luck
a bunker on a golf course is a hazard

explanation.surface: A golfer risking the sand trap in an unplanned way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something random or slapdash is done without method or order.

clue.text: Noble Frenchman at last provides money

indicators.note: last shows the little word goes at the end

parts.note: a duc is a French duke

explanation.surface: A French aristocrat finally pays up.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe, a form of currency.

clue.text: With cover removed, as in reformed dunce

indicators.note: in puts the little word inside the rearranged letters
reformed means the letters of dunce are formed afresh

explanation.surface: A dim pupil exposed after being reformed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' makes UNCED from DUNCE, and 'in' puts AS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken out of its case or casing, so laid bare.

clue.text: Some items, cheap, he 'ticked off, with sound omissions

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone ticking off a list of bargain items.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the end of 'cheap' and finishes inside 'ticked'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphesis is the gradual loss of an unstressed first vowel, as in squire from esquire, a kind of dropped sound.

clue.text: No victory opening, for poem in this tongue

indicators.note: no tells us a letter is to be taken away

parts.note: verse is poetry, a poem

indicators.note: opening picks out the first letter of the word victory

explanation.surface: A poem in a language without a triumphant start.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Chap wrecking taverns. Jeeves, perhaps

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: wrecking smashes the word taverns, so its letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A man smashing up pubs, possibly Wodehouse's valet.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeeves is the gentleman's gentleman in P. G. Wodehouse's stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeeves is a valet, a man employed as a personal servant.
